children: Mediterranean Shipping Co. is discussing the possible acquisition of the roughly 80% stake in Meyer Werft owned by Germany’s federal government and the state of Lower Saxony, Bloomberg News reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the talks.
The negotiations remain preliminary and could end without an agreement. Other bidders also may emerge. Any transaction would include Meyer Werft’s shipyards in Papenburg and Rostock.

For investors, a deal could strengthen MSC’s control over future ship capacity while giving Germany an exit from its 2024 rescue of Meyer Werft. It also would highlight the strategic value of Europe’s limited cruise-ship construction capacity as demand recovers.

The two governments invested €400 million ($459 million) in Meyer Werft and provided €2.6 billion in credit after the pandemic weakened the company’s finances. Officials reportedly want to recover at least their equity investment in a sale.

MSC Cruises is Meyer Werft’s biggest customer. The companies reached a preliminary agreement last year covering four new vessels and options for two more, potentially worth as much as €10 billion. Deliveries are expected to begin in 2030 and could keep the Papenburg yard busy through 2035.
Meyer Werft also builds ships for Carnival
. The company employs about 5,000 people, while its regional supply chain supports more than 20,000 additional jobs.
